title: Arbitrary-prime polynomial resource contract
objective: Specify and test Sage-compatible GF(p)[x] semantics for p at least 2^64 and define a representation-neutral generated-resource protocol owning fmpz_mod_ctx_t plus fmpz_mod_poly_t without caller capacity prediction or cross-resource lifetime coupling

oracles: SageMath 10.9 semantics at primes 2^89-1 and larger

handoff.summary: Defined the arbitrary-prime GF(p)[x] boundary as one self-contained generated owner of both fmpz_mod_ctx_t and fmpz_mod_poly_t. Operands are borrowed only for a synchronous call; each polynomial result is a fresh callee-owned resource with its own equivalent context; division, xgcd, and factor aggregates extract independent child owners; text and serialization use callee-owned variable-size regions; callers never predict capacities. An ordinary CPython fallback proves construction normalization, arithmetic, divrem, monic gcd/xgcd including (0,0), evaluation, and formatting at the Mersenne primes 2^89-1, 2^127-1, and 2^521-1. SageMath 10.9.post1 observations pin explicit cross-parent construction versus binary mismatch, zero factor/roots behavior, factor unit and root multiplicity conventions, and serialization parent identity. The benchmark records the current Sage.js unsigned-word RangeError plus cold and warm Sage reference measurements.
risks: The public finite-field parent currently exists for arbitrary primes, but polynomial.py classifies moduli above 2^64 as legacy and reaches nmod_poly, which rejects them. This lane deliberately does not wire or alter that shared public path.

The fallback factor and roots semantics are pinned, but factorization itself is delegated to future generated fmpz_mod_poly_factor declarations; recreating it in Python would defeat the architecture and performance objective.

The generated FFI schema must ensure extracted aggregate children clone or take ownership of an equivalent context. A child that borrows an aggregate or parent context would violate the no cross-resource lifetime dependency contract.
Windows uses the same-source fallback until its FLINT build exposes the generated resource capability; WebAssembly still needs the same declaration lowered to owned linear-memory state.
next_steps: Independently review the Sage 10.9 observations and the resource lifetime contract before integration.

Add a declaration-schema FmpzModPolynomial resource with construction, copy, coefficient access, arithmetic, divrem, gcd/xgcd, evaluation, formatting, factor/roots, and stable serialization. Keep context plus polynomial as one ownership unit and make all variable-size results callee owned.
Wire polynomial.py only after lifecycle fuzzing proves that closing operands, parent objects, and aggregate result resources cannot invalidate escaped polynomial results.
Add the module to pyrightconfig.json and the focused test to test/node-test-manifest.cjs in the integration lane.
